[0] Apple Pay is the go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in physical stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more useful. Here's how they work.

[1] Redesigned in iOS 27

[2] One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier to switch between different credit cards during the checkout process on websites and in apps.

[3] With the new design, you can swipe directly on the main Apple Pay checkout screen to switch between credit cards. You can also tap on a credit card to view all available Apple Pay credit cards in a grid layout.

[4] The new design also makes it easier to view individual credit card details, including rewards, balances, buy now, pay later options, and more.

[5] iOS 27 is now available in developer and public beta versions, and is expected to officially launch this fall.

[6] American Express Rewards Points

[7] Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that allows you to make payments using American Express Membership Rewards points.

[8] When using an American Express card to shop online or in apps, you'll see a new "Use Points" option that displays your current Membership Rewards points balance. You can use points to pay all or part of your purchase directly within the Apple Pay checkout process.

[9] Amex points redeemed through Apple Pay are worth 0.7 cents each. For example, 10,000 points can be converted into $70 to offset your purchase amount.

[10] Tap to Provision

[11] In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new feature called "Tap to Provision" that works with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store purchases.

[12] This feature is an extension of the iPhone "Tap to Pay" feature, which Apple expects to launch this fall. Apple explains as follows:

[13] With a simple tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant's iPhone to enjoy a more personalized and faster in-store shopping experience, securely sharing email and other contact information, shipping addresses, membership rewards information, and more. Customers can also view the items in their shopping cart in real time, track purchased items, and ensure all discounts and offers are applied correctly.

[14] Once completed, customers can use Apple Pay on their own iPhone to complete the checkout.

[15] Topping Up Debit Cards

[16] Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage their debit card balances directly within the Apple Pay interface.

[17] According to Apple, you can top up supported debit cards directly through Apple Pay, either in Apple Wallet or at checkout.

[18] Summary

[19] As Apple Pay becomes more widespread and adopted by more retailers, it's great to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. Personally, whether shopping online or in physical stores, Apple Pay is basically my go-to payment method.

[20] How often do you use Apple Pay? What is your favorite Apple Pay feature? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
